member.name: M:Sagittaras.Scripting.Activation.IScriptActivator.Release(Sagittaras.Scripting.ITransientEntityScript)
member.summary: Takes back a script that is no longer bound to any entity instance.
member.param: Script dropped by the registry.

remarks.para: Keeps the released scripts and hands them out again instead of letting every spawn allocate. It works because a transient script takes its state in rather than through its constructor - a rented instance is bound to its new entity the same way a fresh one is.

The scripts it holds are the ones already released, so the pool settles at the peak number of entities that lived at once. Pass a capacity where that peak is not something the game keeps a lid on by itself.

This is what a manager uses unless told otherwise, so that transient scripts cost what they should out of the box. A capacity of zero turns the pooling off and every spawn allocates again, which is the way to tell a leftover state apart from a defect while chasing one.
Not safe for concurrent use, the same as the registry that drives it.

member.name: T:Sagittaras.Scripting.Attributes.GameScriptAttribute
member.summary: Marks abstract class as an available and registrable entrypoint.

remarks.para: The marked class is the contract declared by the core module: its virtual members are the hook-points, and every concrete script derived from it is discovered and registered under it. Calls made through are resolved against this base type, which is what keeps the core free of any reference to the extending modules.

Name the hook-points after the moment they open up - OnAggro, OnDamageTaken. Read top to bottom, the marked class is then the list of moments an extending module can step into. A hook-point returning a value asks a question at that moment instead of announcing it: the core hands in what it would have used on its own, and the script answers or passes it back.
Classes without this attribute will not be registered as entrypoint.

member.name: T:Sagittaras.Scripting.Building.IScriptHierarchy
member.summary: Resolves the entrypoints a concrete script can be reached through.

remarks.para: Scripts form a hierarchy of entrypoints - an object script, a world object script derived from it, a creature script derived from that - and the core module calls a hook-point at whichever level it is declared on. A concrete script therefore has to be reachable by every entrypoint above it, not only by the one it derives from directly.

The registries resolve this once during registration and index the script under each of its entrypoints. A call is then a single lookup by the requested type, with no assignability testing left for the game loop.

member.name: T:Sagittaras.Scripting.Building.IScriptRegistryBuilder
member.summary: Collects the scripts of all modules and builds the serving them.

remarks.para: Registration is deliberately the expensive half of the system. Resolving the entrypoints of a script, ordering by priority and capturing how a transient script is created all happen here, once during the boot, so that a hook-point reached from the game loop is a plain lookup.

Discovering the scripts - scanning the assemblies for and the entrypoints - is not a part of the builder. It is a separate concern feeding these methods, so that an environment where reflection is unreliable, such as an AOT build with stripped code, can replace it without touching the registries.

member.name: T:Sagittaras.Scripting.IGameScript
member.summary: General marker interface for scripting extensions.

remarks.para: Game Script allows for wiring custom logic into the core library of your game by providing extensible hook-points for further customization of the behavior.

The core module declares an abstract base script annotated by , whose members are the hook-points it is willing to expose. An extending module derives from that base, overrides only the hook-points it cares about, and the core calls them back through without ever referencing the extension.
This interface is never implemented directly - derive from , or , which differ in what the script is bound to and how long its instance lives.

member.name: T:Sagittaras.Scripting.IGlobalScript
member.summary: Global Script represents extensible hook-points without a specific game entity target.
member.remarks: Use it for hook-points that belong to a system rather than to a single entity - loot rolls, difficulty scaling, save migrations and similar cross-cutting behavior. Every registered implementation of the same base script is a valid target of a call, so a single hook-point may be answered by several extending modules at once.

member.name: T:Sagittaras.Scripting.IScriptManager
member.summary: Represents a global entrypoint for calling and invoking instances of .

remarks.para: The manager is the only place where the core module meets the extending ones. The core reaches its own hook-point by calling Call with the abstract base script as the type argument; the manager resolves the registered implementations and invokes the passed delegate on them. A hook-point with no implementation is not an error - the call simply does nothing and the result-returning overloads fall back to the default value.

Overloads differ only in what the script is bound to: no target for , an entity identity for , and a concrete entity instance for . The manager itself only dispatches - the scripts are held by , and .

member.name: T:Sagittaras.Scripting.ITransientEntityScript
member.summary: Counterpart of - while Entity Script serves all instances of the Entity, Transient Entity Script exists per instance of the Entity.

remarks.para: Because the instance is not shared, the script may keep state of the single entity it was created for - a combat phase, accumulated damage, a spawn timer. The instance is created by and discarded once the entity raises .

Despite the kinship the interface deliberately does not derive from . The two have a different lifecycle and are served by a different registry, and an inheritance between them would let a transient entrypoint satisfy the shared entity calls of - where it would silently find nothing instead of failing to compile.
This interface only marks the script for the storage. The script is always written against , which carries the initialization contract.

member.name: T:Sagittaras.Scripting.ITransientEntityScript`1
member.summary: Transient Entity Script initialized by the arguments its entrypoint offers.

remarks.para: The entrypoint - the abstract base script annotated by - binds once, and every concrete script derived from it inherits that contract. An entrypoint offering nothing but the entity itself binds .

State is taken in rather than through a constructor, so the script can be created by a plain new and, later on, rented from a pool and initialized again. The price is that dependencies cannot be injected through the constructor nor held in readonly fields; a container has to reach the script by property or method injection.

member.typeparam: Arguments offered by the entrypoint. Declare it as a readonly struct - it travels by in reference, so a struct keeps the spawn free of boxing.

member.summary: Creates, serves and discards the instances bound to the individual instances of a scripted entity.

remarks.para: Unlike the other two registries this one changes during the game, as entities spawn and get released. It is not safe for concurrent use - registration, instantiation and calls are expected to happen on the thread owning the game loop.
